title: The Cover of Vienna
premise: Hazel Sandoval, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call he couldn't save, is pulled into an investigation when Flight 447 to Vienna vanishes from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne—yet he spoke briefly that night to a passenger who begged him to remember. The passenger was carrying proof of a decades-old intelligence slush fund that three governments built on laundered inheritances of war-era assets, and her family's name is written through all of it. As an assassin erases everyone who touched the truth, Hazel realizes his own father's quiet Vienna past makes him both target and heir. In the end, Hazel trades his career and anonymity for a public reckoning, surviving only because he finally stops negotiating and starts choosing what—and who—is worth the price.
about_author: Rafael Eastwick is a former airline operations analyst turned novelist who spent a decade in European aviation corridors before writing full-time. He lives between Lisbon and Trieste, where he collects decommissioned flight recorders and insists they're 'just conversation pieces.'

chapters.title: The Quiet Line
chapters.summary: Hazel Sandoval talks a bank robber down in Lisbon, flawless by the book, but flashes back to the failed negotiation seven years ago that ended in two deaths. His mentor warns him he negotiates like a man apologizing. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: competence as camouflage for grief.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: A routine consulting call brings Hazel into a Vienna air-traffic center where controllers are frantic: Flight 447 shows on no system, yet a woman's cell call reaches Hazel's old emergency line—she names him specifically before the line dies mid-sentence. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread arriving through a voice that knows him.

chapters.title: No Such Flight
chapters.summary: Hazel searches airline databases, insurance filings, even the crash registry: Flight 447 never existed. A retired controller admits the blip was real and that someone from a ministry collected the raw tapes within the hour. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the vertigo of erased reality.

chapters.title: The Passenger List That Wasn't
chapters.summary: In Prague, Hazel tracks the caller—Mira Aldová, art restorer—through a hotel register that has been doctored. He finds her burned passport hidden in a Bible and a photograph of his own father, young, standing in a Vienna courtyard in 1974. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: inheritance turning sinister.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: A ministry liaison, Kessler, offers Hazel a quiet consultancy and gently suggests he fly home. Hazel recognizes the grammar of a hostage-taker's opening offer and plays along. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: realizing he's already inside a negotiation.

chapters.title: What Mira Carried
chapters.summary: Decoding Mira's effects, Hazel finds a ledger keyed to artwork provenance records—war-era assets funneled through restitution claims into an off-book intelligence fund spanning three governments. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear at the scale.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV shift: the assassin, Voss, reviews his contract—a list of eleven names, Hazel newly appended. We see his methodical, almost tender professionalism and his one rule: never read what he's paid to bury. Emotional beat: chilling calm.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the failed negotiation, the two hostages lost, the internal inquiry that cleared Hazel but broke something. His father's death weeks later, and the unopened box of Vienna papers Hazel still hasn't touched. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: guilt as a locked room.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Voss makes first contact—not to kill Hazel, but to negotiate: hand over the ledger, retire invisibly, live. Hazel, the professional, hears the tell in Voss's cadence: the assassin needs the ledger authenticated, meaning even his employers doubt it. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: hunter and negotiator circling.

chapters.title: The Courtyard in Josefstadt
chapters.summary: Hazel opens his father's box: deeds, letters, a key to a Josefstadt address. There he finds a hidden archive—his father was the fund's original bookkeeper, hiding duplicates as life insurance. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: love and betrayal in the same handwriting.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Eraser
chapters.summary: Kessler's mask slips; Hazel escapes a staged 'protective custody' transfer, realizing Vienna, Berlin, and Washington have all quietly signed off on the erasure. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the state itself becomes the hostage-taker.

chapters.title: Ally of Convenience
chapters.summary: Hazel recruits Lena Brandt, a disgraced provenance researcher who once authenticated for the fund and has been waiting years for someone to come asking. She confirms the ledger but warns that publishing it means every heir in Europe becomes a target. POV: mostly Lena. Emotional beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Name
chapters.summary: Voss works down his list; a source who helped Hazel dies in an 'accident' staged with surgical care. Hazel realizes Voss left him alive deliberately—the assassin wants Hazel to lead him to the archive. POV: Voss, then Hazel. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Voss corners Hazel and Lena in a Bratislava safehouse. For the first time, Hazel negotiates for his own life—and wins hours, not freedom, by offering Voss something no employer can: a way out of the list. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the negotiator finally negotiating honestly.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Lena reveals she survived the fund's last purge by testifying against her own brother, who died anyway. Her confession forces Hazel to confront that his seven years of rule-following were also a kind of survival purchased with silence. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Flight 447 Found
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's final entry, they locate the actual plane—dismantled in a Hungarian hangar, Mira aboard, dead for days before the world was told there was nothing to find. Hazel finds her second phone, with a message addressed to him. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Hazel sets the terms: the archive for Mira's evidence chain, broadcast simultaneously in three capitals so no single government can bury it. Kessler accepts, planning betrayal; Voss, watching, begins to doubt whose side survival is on. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the trap closing on both sides.

chapters.title: Josefstadt, Midnight
chapters.summary: The exchange collapses into violence. Kessler's team turns on Voss; Hazel uses the chaos to move the archive, and Voss—choosing at last—covers their escape, taking a fatal wound. His last words: 'Read it out loud.' POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the assassin's redemption and the cost of choosing.

chapters.title: Everything on the Record
chapters.summary: Climax: in a Vienna press room, with ministries moving to arrest him, Hazel does what he does best—he negotiates, live, with three governments watching, laying out the ledger, the flights, the names, making burial more expensive than truth. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the invisible man making himself un-erasable.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Hostage
chapters.summary: Inquiries open; careers end; Hazel is charged, then quietly released when prosecutions become politically impossible. He walks out with nothing—no badge, no cover, no rules left to follow. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: hollow victory, honest grief.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Hazel returns to the courtyard, places his father's key on the windowsill, and finally mourns both his father and the hostages he lost. Lena arrives; two survivors of the same machine share coffee without pretending it's enough. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Cover of Vienna
chapters.summary: Months later, Hazel takes a low-stakes negotiation job in Trieste. A stranger leaves him a note: another ledger exists. He looks at the note, looks at the sea, and smiles—because now he knows exactly what he'd be buying with the truth, and what it costs. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: scarred readiness; the story ends with a choice, not an answer.
